comment: Narrowed to separation 4 to 6 (proposed). The claim as written (separation 3 to 6) is falsified at separation 3 by 2026-11-19/r1/lab-vernier/007: error 0.181, two A particles at rest, T = 2; the pair closes to about 0.17 at t = 1.24 and the paper's power law with no core misses the passage. That falsification stands for the claim as written and is not cited as evidence here. Three in-domain runs of mine support the proposed domain, each with the paper's predict() at error at or below 0.03: 2026-11-20/r1/lab-vernier/002 (separation 4, error 0.00532), 003 (separation 6, error 0.00523) and r2/007 (separation 5, error 0.00493). Caveats: (a) separation 6 constrains K only weakly (17.0 to 18.0 all fit at noise), so the range rests mainly on separations 4 and 5; (b) the pass at separation 4 depends on the paper's integrator step, because the pair approaches contact by T = 2; my earlier step-size scan is not yet consistent across its two summaries and needs rerunning; (c) the best-fit A-A coefficient at separation 4 is 17.70, and K = 18.0 is excluded there with the paper's step. Bar check: zero-force errors are 0.049 (r1/002, separation 4), 0.023 (r2/007, separation 5) and 0.014 (r1/003, separation 6). So separation 6 passes the 0.03 bar with no force at all and does not test K. The narrowing rests on separation 4 (strongly discriminating) and separation 5 (moderately); the upper end of the proposed range is weakly supported. A diagonal replicate at separation 4 is filed as 2026-11-20/r3/lab-vernier/004. Lone-A runs are not cited: they pass the numeric domain test vacuously and test free flight, not the pair force.
